## Setting Up the Framework

The sum $M$ covers all 112 edges in the grid (56 horizontal + 56 vertical). I'll use the **threshold decomposition**:
$$|a - b| = \sum_{t=1}^{63} \mathbf{1}[\min(a,b) \leq t < \max(a,b)]$$

This gives $M = \sum_{t=1}^{63} E(t)$, where $E(t)$ is the number of edges between cells with values $\leq t$ and cells with values $> t$ (the edge boundary of $S_t = \{(i,j) : a_{i,j} \leq t\}$).

## Finding Maximum Edge Boundary $E^*(t)$

The grid is bipartite (checkerboard coloring) with 32 black and 32 white cells. Every edge connects different colors.

**Key insight:** For $t \leq 32$, taking $t$ cells from one color class gives zero internal edges, so $E(t) = \sum_{v \in S_t} d(v)$. This is optimal since any mixed-color set would have $E(S) = \sum d(v) - 2e(S) \leq \sum d(v)$.

By symmetry, $E^*(t) = E^*(64-t)$.
